items.topic: Gait belt — snug over clothing; fingers fit underneath; nonskid footwear
items.stem: The nurse prepares to ambulate an unsteady adult client with a gait belt. Which action is correct?

options.text: Apply the gait belt snugly over clothing around the waist so fingers can fit underneath, and ensure nonskid footwear
Apply the gait belt directly on bare skin as tightly as possible with no finger space
Skip footwear because the belt alone prevents falls
Place the belt loosely around the chest over the breasts

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: place gait belt snugly over a layer of clothing with two fingers fitting between belt and client; ensure nonslip footwear. Open RN (NCBI): apply gait belt on top of clothing/gown and snugly over clothing with proper footwear such as nonslip socks or shoes.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Belt goes over clothing to protect skin; it should allow finger space for safe hold, not maximum tightness on bare skin.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Both sources emphasize nonskid/nonslip footwear before ambulation or transfer.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Gait belts are placed around the waist, not loosely around the chest.

sources.title: 9.3 Transferring Patients
sources.evidence: Nonslip footwear; belt snug over clothing; two fingers fit.

items.topic: Cane — hold on stronger (opposite) side of weak limb
items.stem: A client with left leg weakness is learning to walk with a single-point cane. Which teaching point is correct?

options.text: Hold the cane in the right (stronger) hand so it moves with the weaker left leg
Always hold the cane in the left hand next to the weak leg
Carry the cane in both hands in front of the body
Use the cane only when sitting, never when walking

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: hold the cane in the opposite hand of the weak or painful limb; cane moves with the affected leg. Open RN Nursing Assistant: place the cane on the stronger side.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Holding the cane on the weak side reduces the widened base of support that opposite-hand use provides.
rationales.C: Incorrect. A single cane is held in one hand for balance and support during gait.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Canes are assistive devices for ambulation/balance when walking.

sources.title: 9.3 Transferring Patients
sources.evidence: Hold cane opposite weak/painful limb; moves with affected leg.

items.topic: NGN matrix — sensory overload: reduce noise/lights; earplugs; quiet supportive environment
items.stem: An older adult in a monitored unit becomes agitated amid continuous alarms, bright lights, and frequent interruptions. For each intervention, indicate whether it is Indicated or Not indicated to reduce sensory overload.

rows.text: Dim lights and reduce unnecessary noise when safe
Offer earplugs or headphones to limit auditory overload
Keep the environment continuously loud to maintain alertness
Provide a calmer, quieter setting with orientation cues as able

rationales.R1: Indicated. OpenStax: dim lights and reduce noise levels to minimize sensory input.
rationales.R2: Indicated. OpenStax: provide earplugs or headphones; ICU exemplar used earplugs/noise-canceling headphones.
rationales.R3: Not indicated. Increasing noise worsens overload; Merck delirium care uses a quiet, stable environment.
rationales.R4: Indicated. OpenStax supports calming supportive environment; Merck: stable, quiet, well-lit setting with orientation cues.

sources.title: 29.2 Impaired Sensory Function
sources.evidence: Dim lights, reduce noise, earplugs/headphones; calming environment.

sources.title: Delirium
sources.evidence: Stable, quiet, well-lit environment with visual orientation cues.

items.topic: RSV — Contact Precautions for duration of illness (infants/young children)
items.client_needs_subcategory: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
items.stem: An infant is admitted with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis. Which isolation plan is appropriate?

options.text: Contact Precautions for the duration of illness, with gown and gloves for patient-care contact
Airborne Precautions only in a negative-pressure room with N95 for all staff
No transmission-based precautions beyond Standard Precautions
Droplet Precautions only until the first afebrile hour

rationales.A: Correct. CDC Appendix A: RSV in infants, young children, and immunocompromised adults — Contact + Standard for duration of illness. OpenStax: Contact Precautions use gown and gloves for direct/indirect contact pathogens.
rationales.B: Incorrect. CDC lists Contact (not Airborne) for RSV in this population.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Transmission-based Contact Precautions are indicated for RSV in infants/young children.
rationales.D: Incorrect. CDC duration is duration of illness for Contact Precautions, not a one-hour fever rule.

sources.evidence: RSV: Contact + Standard; duration of illness.

items.topic: Impetigo — Contact Precautions until 24 hours after effective therapy
items.client_needs_subcategory: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
items.stem: A school-age child is admitted with widespread impetigo and started on effective antimicrobial therapy. Which precaution guidance is correct?

options.text: Use Contact Precautions until 24 hours after initiation of effective therapy
Use Airborne Precautions for 7 days after the rash appears
Discontinue all precautions immediately when therapy is ordered, before the first dose
Use only Droplet Precautions without gown or gloves

rationales.A: Correct. CDC Appendix A: Impetigo — Contact + Standard until 24 hours after initiation of effective therapy. OpenStax: Contact Precautions include gown and gloves for contact-transmitted infections.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Impetigo is not managed with Airborne Precautions per CDC Appendix A.
rationales.C: Incorrect. CDC continues Contact Precautions until 24 hours after effective therapy starts.
rationales.D: Incorrect. CDC specifies Contact Precautions for impetigo.

items.topic: Enoxaparin — do not expel air bubble; subcutaneous abdomen; do not rub
items.stem: A client will self-inject enoxaparin from a prefilled syringe at home. Which instruction is essential?

options.text: Do not expel the air bubble before injection; inject subcutaneously in the abdomen and do not rub the site
Expel all air from the syringe, then inject intramuscularly into the deltoid
Inject through clothing into any bruised area to hide the site
Massage the site vigorously for 5 minutes after each dose

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax and DailyMed Lovenox: avoid ejecting/expelling the air bubble; inject into abdominal wall sites; do not rub after injection.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Expelling the air bubble can lose drug; route is subcutaneous, not IM deltoid.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Both sources: do not inject through clothing or into bruised/scarred skin.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Rubbing increases bruising risk; teaching is not to rub.

sources.evidence: Avoid ejecting air bubble; SQ abdomen; avoid rubbing.

sources.publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
sources.evidence: Do not expel air bubble; abdominal wall sites; do not rub.

items.topic: NGN cloze — ACE inhibitor angioedema: stop drug; seek emergency care for face/tongue swelling
items.stem: A client starts lisinopril for hypertension. Complete the teaching using the drop-down choices.

ngn.template: Teach the client that a serious adverse effect of ACE inhibitors is {B1}. If swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat occurs, the client should {B2} and {B3}. ACE inhibitors are also {B4} in pregnancy.

B2.text: stop the ACE inhibitor and seek emergency care
wait one week before calling anyone

B3.text: treat airway swelling as an emergency because oropharyngeal angioedema can be fatal
restart the drug once swelling decreases slightly
take an extra dose with food

rationales.B1a: Correct. OpenStax and Merck list angioedema as a serious ACE inhibitor adverse effect.
rationales.B1b: Incorrect. Photosensitivity is not the key ACEI safety teaching here.
rationales.B1c: Incorrect. Not an ACEI hallmark adverse effect.
rationales.B1d: Incorrect. Not associated with ACE inhibitors.
rationales.B2a: Correct. Prior angioedema is a contraindication; stop the drug and seek urgent care for swelling.
rationales.B2b: Incorrect. Increasing the dose worsens risk.
rationales.B2c: Incorrect. Potassium supplements increase hyperkalemia risk with ACEIs.
rationales.B2d: Incorrect. Airway-threatening angioedema requires immediate care.
rationales.B3a: Correct. Merck: angioedema affecting the oropharynx can be fatal.
rationales.B3b: Incorrect. Tongue/airway swelling is an emergency.
rationales.B3c: Incorrect. History of ACEI angioedema contraindicates rechallenge.
rationales.B3d: Incorrect. Not a treatment for angioedema.
rationales.B4a: Correct. OpenStax and Merck: ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy.
rationales.B4b: Incorrect. ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy, not preferred first-line then.
rationales.B4c: Incorrect. Pregnancy is a contraindication; ACE inhibitors are not required therapy in pregnancy.
rationales.B4d: Incorrect. Fetal harm risk means they are not harmless in pregnancy.

sources.title: 18.2 Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) Inhibitors
sources.evidence: Angioedema; contraindicated in pregnancy; prior angioedema contraindication.

sources.title: Medications for Hypertension
sources.evidence: Angioedema most serious; oropharynx can be fatal; contraindicated in pregnancy.

items.topic: Infant dehydration — sunken fontanelle/eyes are warning signs needing prompt care
items.stem: A parent of a 6-month-old with gastroenteritis asks which finding means the infant needs prompt medical evaluation for dehydration. Which finding should the nurse emphasize?

options.text: Sunken soft spot (fontanelle) and sunken eyes
One loose stool with normal wet diapers and tears
Brief spit-up after feeding with a moist mouth
Occasional hiccups after burping

rationales.A: Correct. CPS Caring for Kids lists sunken fontanelle and sunken eyes among dehydration warning signs needing medical advice. Merck: moderate dehydration includes sunken eyes and fontanelles.
rationales.B: Incorrect. CPS notes healthy children may have an occasional loose stool without dehydration danger when other signs are absent.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Isolated spit-up with moist mucosa is not a dehydration red flag.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Hiccups are not a dehydration indicator.

items.topic: Childhood lead — blood test is how exposure is detected; older housing paint dust risk
items.stem: A community nurse teaches caregivers of toddlers living in aging housing about lead exposure. Which statement is the priority teaching point?

options.text: A blood lead test is the best way to know if a child has been exposed; peeling paint dust in older homes is an important risk
Lead exposure always causes an obvious bright red rash, so testing is unnecessary if the skin looks normal
Only outdoor soil matters; indoor paint dust cannot affect children
Home sanding of old paint is the safest way to remove lead without professional advice

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: blood lead test is the best way to detect exposure; children often have no obvious symptoms; older housing paint dust is a key source. Health Canada: babies/small children ingest household dust including from lead-based paints; older homes more likely painted with lead-based paint.
rationales.B: Incorrect. CDC: most children with lead in blood have no obvious immediate symptoms.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Health Canada and CDC describe indoor paint dust as an important pathway for young children.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Health Canada warns mechanical removal/sanding can release hazardous lead dust.

items.topic: Therapeutic communication — abruptly changing the subject is nontherapeutic
items.stem: A client begins crying while describing fear about a new cancer diagnosis. Which nurse response is nontherapeutic?

options.text: "Let's not talk about that—tell me what you want for lunch instead."
"This sounds frightening. What worries you most right now?"
Sitting quietly for a moment, then saying, "I'm here with you; go on when you are ready."
"Help me understand what the diagnosis means for you."

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax PMH: changing the subject is a barrier that can feel insensitive. Open RN Nursing Assistant: changing the subject blocks communication and conveys lack of empathy.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Open-ended exploration of feelings is therapeutic.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Silence/presence supporting the client is therapeutic.

items.jurisdiction_note: CNO Consent practice guideline (July 2025) interpreting Ontario HCCA requirements for informed consent.
items.topic: CNO Consent — informed consent includes nature, benefits, risks, alternatives, consequences of refusal
items.stem: Before a planned invasive procedure in Ontario, the nurse reviews whether consent is informed. Which set of information must have been provided for consent to be considered informed under CNO guidance?

options.text: Nature of the treatment, expected benefits, material risks and side effects, alternative courses of action, and likely consequences of not having the treatment
Only the scheduled time of the procedure, without discussion of risks or alternatives
A guarantee that no adverse effects are possible
The nurse’s personal preference about whether the client should proceed

rationales.A: Correct. CNO Consent guideline: informed consent requires information a reasonable person would need, including nature, expected benefits, material risks/side effects, alternatives, and likely consequences of not having the treatment.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Scheduling alone does not meet informed-consent content requirements.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Material risks must be disclosed; guarantees of no adverse effects are not the standard.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Consent must be voluntary and free of misrepresentation; the nurse’s personal preference is not the required content.

sources.title: Consent practice guideline
sources.evidence: Nature; benefits; material risks/side effects; alternatives; consequences of not having treatment.

items.topic: NGN bowtie — septic shock: early fluids, cultures, antibiotics; monitor lactate/perfusion
items.stem: A hospitalized adult develops fever, confusion, tachycardia, and hypotension concerning for septic shock. Complete the bowtie: most likely condition, two priority actions, and two parameters to monitor.

conditions.text: Septic shock from dysregulated response to infection with hypoperfusion

actions.text: Obtain cultures and start prompt broad-spectrum antibiotics
Begin aggressive IV fluid resuscitation per sepsis protocol
Delay all fluids until cultures return in 72 hours
Give only oral acetaminophen and reassess next week

parameters.text: Blood pressure / MAP and perfusion response after fluids (and pressors if needed)
Serum lactate and ongoing organ perfusion indicators (e.g., urine output)
Fashion preference for hospital gown color
Number of visitors on the unit whiteboard only

rationales.K1: Incorrect. Allergic rhinitis does not explain hypotension and organ hypoperfusion.
rationales.K2: Correct. Merck/OpenStax: septic shock is sepsis with persistent hypotension/hypoperfusion related to infection.
rationales.K3: Incorrect. Headache alone does not match this shock picture.
rationales.K4: Incorrect. Localized bruise is not systemic septic shock.
rationales.A1: Correct. Merck: collect cultures then give prompt empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics; OpenStax one-hour bundle includes cultures and antibiotics.
rationales.A2: Correct. Merck and OpenStax: aggressive IV fluid resuscitation is foundational; vasopressors if hypotension persists.
rationales.A3: Incorrect. Delaying fluids for culture results increases mortality risk.
rationales.A4: Incorrect. Septic shock requires urgent inpatient/ICU-level care.
rationales.A5: Incorrect. Antipyretic alone is not sepsis resuscitation.
rationales.P1: Correct. OpenStax targets MAP ~65 mm Hg with fluids/vasopressors; monitor perfusion response.
rationales.P2: Correct. OpenStax bundle includes lactate; Merck monitors lactate and urine output as perfusion markers.
rationales.P3: Incorrect. Irrelevant to septic shock monitoring.

items.topic: Lead exposure teaching SATA — blood test; older paint dust; avoid sanding; children often asymptomatic
items.stem: Which teaching points about childhood lead exposure are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: A blood lead test is the best way to determine whether a child has been exposed
Children may have lead in their blood without obvious immediate symptoms
Peeling lead-based paint dust in older homes is an important exposure pathway for young children
Dry sanding old lead paint at home is the preferred first action for families
Young children are at higher risk because of hand-to-mouth behavior and floor-level exposure
Lead exposure is impossible if the child has never left the city limits

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: blood lead test is the best way to know exposure.
rationales.B: Correct. CDC: most children with lead in blood have no obvious immediate symptoms.
rationales.C: Correct. CDC and Health Canada identify paint dust in older homes as a key pathway.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Health Canada: mechanical removal/sanding can release hazardous lead dust.
rationales.E: Correct. Health Canada: hand-to-mouth activity and low breathing zone increase risk.
rationales.F: Incorrect. Lead sources exist indoors (paint, dust, products) regardless of city limits.

items.topic: Postoperative DVT prevention — early and frequent ambulation
items.stem: On the first postoperative day after major abdominal surgery, which nursing action best helps prevent deep vein thrombosis?

options.text: Promote early and frequent ambulation as soon as the client is cleared to mobilize
Keep the client on strict bed rest for one week without leg movement
Limit all fluids to concentrate the blood
Elevate only the head of the bed and avoid moving the legs

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: early and frequent ambulation stimulates blood flow and avoids stasis. Merck DVT prevention: ambulation and prevention of immobility are core preventive measures.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Fluid restriction to concentrate blood is not a DVT prevention strategy.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Leg movement/ambulation is needed to reduce venous stasis.
